meta.name: CyRECS911 Attack Matrix (ATT&CK-style)
principles: Matrix is adversary-technique focused (no mitigations, no response steps).
Operational guidance lives in playbooks/ (detection, containment, recovery).
Each technique links to a playbook when available.

sources.path: evidence/Updated - NG911 Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment - 4.1.docx

tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to gather information about NG9-1-1 / PSAP services, endpoints, trust relationships, and exposed interfaces prior to exploitation.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to gain an initial foothold into NG9-1-1 / PSAP environments (people, public-facing services, or trusted relationships).

techniques.name: Phishing leading to PSAP workstation compromise
techniques.summary: Social-engineering delivers malware or credential theft that establishes a foothold on PSAP user endpoints.
attack_mechanics: Spearphishing email/chat leading to payload execution or credential capture
Session/token theft to access PSAP applications and backend services
Follow-on deployment of remote access tooling
techniques.immediate_effect: Compromised endpoint provides access to PSAP applications and adjacent network resources.
techniques.operational_impact: Loss of confidentiality (incident/caller data), loss of integrity of dispatch workflows, increased risk of ransomware/impact operations.

techniques.name: Compromised vendor software/firmware in NG911 components
techniques.summary: Adversary abuses trusted supplier updates or embedded components to introduce malicious code into NG911 functional elements.
attack_mechanics: Malicious update package delivered through vendor channel
Trojanized component/firmware enabling backdoor access
Abuse of trust relationships (signing, update infrastructure)
techniques.immediate_effect: Trusted component executes adversary code within NG9-1-1 operational boundary.
techniques.operational_impact: Stealthy long-term access, integrity compromise of routing/location/call handling, potential broad multi-site disruption.

techniques.name: Legacy ingress via LNG/LPG protocol conversion path
techniques.summary: Adversary leverages legacy-to-i3 conversion points to inject malformed or hostile legacy signaling into the ESInet service plane.
attack_mechanics: Crafted legacy signaling reaches LNG and is translated onward
Boundary assumptions bypassed during protocol conversion
Edge-case parsing triggers unexpected behavior or overload
techniques.immediate_effect: Hostile signaling enters i3-adjacent service path through conversion layer.
techniques.operational_impact: Potential call setup failures, misrouting, media negotiation failures, or DoS effects on gateways and dependent PSAPs.

tactics.name: Identity Manipulation
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to spoof, masquerade, or forge identities and trust assertions used by NG9-1-1 call routing, location, and boundary functions.

techniques.name: SIP caller identity spoofing via INVITE header manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversary forges SIP identity-related fields to misrepresent caller identity/ANI or amplify fraud/swatting/TDoS behaviors.
attack_mechanics: Manipulation of From / P-Asserted-Identity / Remote-Party-ID headers
Unsigned, invalid, or replayed SIP Identity assertions
High-rate identity-varied INVITEs to evade naive filters
techniques.immediate_effect: Call identity trust is violated at ingress and/or during routing decisions.
techniques.operational_impact: Fraud, swatting, false attribution, increased dispatcher workload, and potential incident misprioritization.
techniques.evidence: ThreatModel: caller spoofing; NG-SEC signaling abuse.

techniques.name: LIS impersonation and forged PIDF-LO/location assertions
techniques.summary: Adversary masquerades as LIS or forges location objects/tokens to influence routing and dispatch decisions.
attack_mechanics: Fake LIS endpoint identity presented to clients/services
Forged PIDF-LO objects (location-by-value) delivered to downstream services
Replay or substitution of previously valid location assertions
techniques.immediate_effect: Downstream entities consume untrusted or forged location information.
techniques.operational_impact: Misrouting to incorrect PSAP, dispatch to wrong location, increased call handling time and public safety risk.

tactics.name: Protocol Abuse
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to exploit weaknesses or edge cases in NG9-1-1 signaling and media protocols (SIP, RTP, TLS) including downgrade and negotiation manipulation.

techniques.name: TLS downgrade / weak protocol negotiation on ESInet services
techniques.summary: Adversary coerces weak cryptographic negotiation or exploits insecure protocol configurations to observe or manipulate traffic.
attack_mechanics: Handshake manipulation to prefer weaker versions/ciphers when misconfigured
Opportunistic interception where endpoints allow insecure fallback
Exploit of inconsistent TLS policies across service mesh
techniques.immediate_effect: Reduced transport security and increased susceptibility to interception/modification.
techniques.operational_impact: Confidentiality loss of call metadata/location, integrity risk to routing queries, increased blast radius for follow-on attacks.

techniques.name: Media path compromise via RTP/SRTP negotiation and injection
techniques.summary: Adversary injects, captures, or manipulates call media where SRTP is absent, mis-negotiated, or bridged insecurely.
attack_mechanics: Unauthenticated RTP stream injection into call leg
Media sniffing on unencrypted RTP segments
Codec/SDP parameter abuse to trigger media handling edge cases
techniques.immediate_effect: Call audio/media confidentiality and integrity are compromised.
techniques.operational_impact: Eavesdropping, audio tampering, evidentiary integrity loss, degraded call quality affecting operations.

tactics.name: Data Manipulation
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to corrupt, poison, or insert false data affecting location validation, routing, and operational decision-making.

techniques.name: GIS/LVF dataset poisoning affecting validation and routing
techniques.summary: Adversary modifies authoritative GIS/LVF datasets to cause incorrect validation outcomes and downstream routing errors.
attack_mechanics: Unauthorized edits to GIS/LVF records
Poisoned updates introduced through weak change control
Subtle boundary/value shifts that evade cursory review
techniques.immediate_effect: Validation decisions and derived routing inputs become incorrect.
techniques.operational_impact: Misrouting, delayed dispatch, incorrect jurisdiction selection, cascading operational confusion.

techniques.name: Location record tampering or injection in LIS data stores
techniques.summary: Adversary alters or inserts location records to influence routing/dispatch and to create persistent data integrity issues.
attack_mechanics: Direct modification of LIS data store contents
Insertion of bogus location-by-reference pointers
Inconsistency creation between location-by-value and location-by-reference
techniques.immediate_effect: Location queries resolve to attacker-influenced or inconsistent results.
techniques.operational_impact: Misrouting, incorrect dispatch location, repeated revalidation cycles increasing call handling latency.

tactics.name: Service Disruption
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to degrade availability of NG9-1-1 services, signaling, and dependent gateways through floods, exhaustion, or induced isolation.

techniques.name: TDoS via SIP INVITE/call floods against BCF/ESRP/PSAP queues
techniques.summary: Adversary generates high-rate SIP call attempts to exhaust resources and disrupt call processing.
attack_mechanics: Sustained INVITE floods with varied identifiers
OPTIONS/REGISTER bursts to exhaust signaling processing
Distributed sources to bypass simple per-IP throttles
techniques.immediate_effect: Queue saturation and signaling thread exhaustion on ingress/routing components.
techniques.operational_impact: Call setup delays, call drops, inability to accept emergency calls, degraded situational awareness.

techniques.name: LIS/LVF query flooding to exhaust location and validation services
techniques.summary: Adversary floods LIS/LVF/ECRF queries to degrade capacity and increase routing latency.
attack_mechanics: High-rate API/query requests from compromised or spoofed clients
Repeated revalidation attempts to amplify computational load
Burst patterns aligned with peak operational periods
techniques.immediate_effect: Service capacity exhaustion and increased response time/timeouts.
techniques.operational_impact: Routing delays, failed validations, increased call handling time, possible call failures under load.

techniques.name: Induced isolation of legacy-dependent PSAPs via LPG/LNG failure
techniques.summary: Adversary causes outages or overload at gateways such that PSAPs dependent on legacy interfaces become isolated.
attack_mechanics: Flooding or resource exhaustion targeting LPG/LNG
Triggering crash/fail states through malformed inputs
Exploitation of brittle failover configurations
techniques.immediate_effect: Gateway degradation or failure isolates dependent call paths.
techniques.operational_impact: Loss of service for legacy-dependent jurisdictions, forced fallback procedures, increased risk during transition.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to collect sensitive NG9-1-1 information such as caller location, call media, logs, and incident records.

techniques.name: Bulk collection of caller location and call log datasets
techniques.summary: Adversary gathers sensitive location/call records from LIS/PSAP/logging stores for later exfiltration or misuse.
attack_mechanics: Abuse of legitimate export/reporting functions
Query scraping through automated client access
Log harvesting from centralized logging services
techniques.immediate_effect: Sensitive datasets are aggregated by the adversary inside the environment.
techniques.operational_impact: Privacy harm, operational security exposure, potential targeting of callers/first responders.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to directly affect availability and operational continuity, including destructive actions like ransomware.

techniques.name: Ransomware impacting PSAP workstations and supporting servers
techniques.summary: Adversary encrypts or disables PSAP endpoints/services to halt emergency operations and force recovery actions.
attack_mechanics: File/system encryption on PSAP endpoints
Disruption of CAD/dispatch support systems
Destruction or tampering with backups and recovery paths
techniques.immediate_effect: PSAP operational tooling becomes unavailable or unreliable.
techniques.operational_impact: Severe service interruption, manual fallback operations, delayed response, broad public safety impact.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: Techniques adversaries use to maintain long-term presence in NG9-1-1 environments across restarts, updates, and operator remediation.
